home.title: See how the electoral roll changed, and check every number yourself
home.lede: ElectraLens compares published versions of the electoral roll, flags unusual patterns with an open statistical method, and anchors every publication so anyone can confirm nothing was changed afterwards.
home.is1: A public record of how published rolls changed between versions.
home.is2: An open method that flags patterns worth a closer look, with the evidence and innocent explanations side by side.
home.is3: Publications that two different people approve and that anyone can verify independently.
home.isNot1: Not the Election Commission, and not an official source.
home.isNot2: Not a way to look up or report any individual voter.
home.isNot3: Not proof of wrongdoing: an unusual pattern is a reason to look closer.
home.toolsTitle: What would you like to do?
home.toolFindingsText: Unusual patterns, each with its evidence, alternatives and limits.
home.toolCompareText: Additions, deletions and corrections from state down to part.
home.toolVerifyText: Recompute the hashes in your browser and check the chain.
home.toolClaimsText: Test a number you heard against the published data.
home.toolBoothsText: Search booths by area and print QR posters.
home.toolAssistantText: Registration, forms and official services in plain words.
home.how1Text: Two versions of a roll are ingested and checked; each gets a Merkle root.
home.how2Text: Twelve versioned rules test every part against similar parts.
home.how3Text: A reviewer and a publisher, neither the analyst, approve the exact manifest.
home.how4Text: The manifest hash goes on-chain and into Bitcoin, so it can't be changed quietly.
home.tamperTitle: Change one number. Watch the proof refuse it.
home.tamperText: Every publication is fixed by a hash that is anchored where nobody can quietly edit it. Load a copy into your browser, change any figure and see exactly which row broke.
home.ctaTitle: Every figure here can be checked by anyone.
home.ctaText: Download the files, recompute the hashes, read the chain. You don’t have to trust us.

methodology.title: Methodology {version}
methodology.lede: Every rule, threshold and statistical test behind the findings. Versions are frozen once used, so any finding can be traced to the exact parameters.
methodology.signalLede: Statistical rules compare each part with similar parts. A finding is reported only when it is both rare and large enough to matter.
methodology.dataQualityRow: Record-level checks (R01–R04, R07, R08, R10) report data quality, not a statistical signal.
methodology.test1: Baseline: each part is compared with the other parts of its constituency. Unusual parts are trimmed before the baseline is estimated, so one extreme part can't hide another.
methodology.test2: Spread: a beta-binomial model with a robust dispersion estimate allows for the normal variation between parts.
methodology.test3: Many tests: every part is tested, so p-values are corrected with the Benjamini–Hochberg procedure (q-values) to control false discoveries at {fdr}.
methodology.test4: Uncertainty: rates come with Wilson 95% intervals. Gender comparisons use Fisher’s exact test; deletion reasons use a binomial test per reason with a Bonferroni correction.
methodology.test5: Small parts: parts with fewer than {min} electors are not tested statistically.
methodology.limit1: Statistics show how unusual a pattern is, not why it happened.
methodology.limit2: Deletion reasons are used as recorded and are not checked independently.
methodology.limit3: Name matching across spellings is approximate.
methodology.limit4: Thresholds were tuned on synthetic data only and will be reviewed with real data.
methodology.benchmarkLede: Measured against the anomalies the generator injected, including innocent look-alikes. No accuracy target is claimed for real data.
methodology.benchmarkEmpty: No benchmark is attached to the latest publication.

rulesAbout.R01: Identical entries in the same part.
rulesAbout.R02: Entries with similar names, the same relative’s name and close ages.
rulesAbout.R03: Ages outside the possible range on the qualifying date.
rulesAbout.R04: Ages that changed more than the time between the rolls.
rulesAbout.R05: Deletion rate far above similar parts.
rulesAbout.R06: Addition rate far above similar parts.
rulesAbout.R07: Large transfers into one part, mostly from one other part.
rulesAbout.R08: Unusually many electors at one address.
rulesAbout.R09: Women deleted at a very different rate from men.
rulesAbout.R10: Many entries with missing details or deletions with no reason.
rulesAbout.R11: One deletion reason far more common than in similar parts.
rulesAbout.R12: Unusually many new 18–19 year old electors.

publications.title: Publications
publications.lede: Every publication in every series, in order. Corrections add a new version; retractions are recorded, never deleted.

publication.title: {series}, number {sequence}
publication.manifestHelp: The manifest lists everything this publication covers. Its SHA-256 hash, computed over the RFC 8785 canonical form, is what was anchored.
publication.approvalsHelp: Two different people approved this exact manifest; neither ran the analysis. Names are not published.
publication.anchorsHelp: Independent timestamps of the manifest hash.
publication.downloadsHelp: Each file’s SHA-256 hash is in the manifest, so you can check that a download is exactly what was published.

verify.title: Verify a publication
verify.lede: Your browser downloads the published files, recomputes their hashes and reads the anchor directly from the blockchain. Nothing is taken on trust from our servers.
verify.fileTitle: Check a manifest you already have
verify.fileHelp: If someone sent you a manifest file, check it against our publication record. The file never leaves your device.
verify.proves1: The files you downloaded are byte-for-byte the ones that were published.
verify.proves2: The manifest was anchored at the time shown and has not been changed since.
verify.proves3: The analysis can be traced to exact data roots, code and parameters.
verify.doesNotProve1: That the source rolls themselves are correct.
verify.doesNotProve2: That any finding is right, or explains why a pattern happened.
verify.empty: Nothing has been published yet, so there is nothing to verify.

tamper.title: Change one number and watch the proof break
tamper.lede: A local copy of {series} number {sequence}’s aggregates is loaded into your browser. Edit any value: the file hash stops matching the anchored manifest, and the Merkle tree shows exactly which row changed.
tamper.syntheticOnly: The tamper demo runs only on synthetic publications.
tamper.localOnly: Everything happens in your browser. Nothing you change is sent anywhere.

claims.title: Check a claim about the roll
claims.lede: Heard a number about additions or deletions? Put it in the form and we’ll compare it with the published data, showing exactly which figure we used.
claims.recentEmpty: No claims have been published yet.
claims.how1: The claim is matched to one published figure: an area, a measure and a revision.
claims.how2: Counts within 1% (or 10 people) and percentages within half a point are “consistent”.
claims.how3: Claims about why something happened, or about anyone’s intent, can’t be established from roll data.

form7.body: Form 7 asks for an entry to be removed, for example after a death or a permanent move. Objections are checked by the Electoral Registration Officer before anything is changed.

about.title: An open, checkable look at electoral-roll revisions
about.lede: ElectraLens is an independent project. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by or acting for the Election Commission of India.
about.why: Rolls are revised constantly. Large changes are often routine, sometimes errors, and occasionally something worth asking about. ElectraLens makes those changes visible with a method anyone can read, run and check.
about.p1: Rules, thresholds and code are public and versioned. Every finding links to the exact version used.
about.p2: Every finding carries its innocent explanations and limits, as prominently as its evidence.
about.p3: Nothing is published unless two different people, neither of them the analyst, approve the exact manifest.
about.p4: Publications are anchored on a public blockchain and in Bitcoin through OpenTimestamps.
about.p5: Only aggregates are public. There is no search by person, and small counts are hidden.
about.demo: Everything shown in this demonstration is synthetic: real state and district names give context, but every constituency, part, polling station and person is fictional, and constituencies are numbered from 901 so they cannot be mistaken for real ones.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.lede: What we collect, what we never collect, and how long we keep it.
privacy.never1: Voter ID (EPIC) numbers, or any search by person.
privacy.never2: Your location. Booth pages opened from a QR code are not linked to anyone.
privacy.never3: Advertising or tracking cookies. There is no analytics service.
privacy.rowAccount: Email address (only if you create an account)
privacy.rowAccountWhy: Sign-in and the alerts you ask for
privacy.rowSavedKept: Until you remove them or delete your account
privacy.rowIp: A one-way hash of your IP address when you submit a claim
privacy.cookies: One cookie remembers your language. If you sign in, session cookies keep you signed in. Nothing else.
privacy.delete: You can delete your account, saved items, subscriptions and unpublished claims at any time from your account settings.

verdictHelp.MISMATCH: Something does not match what was published. Do not rely on these files.

verdictHelp.RETRACTED: This publication was retracted. Its files can still be checked, but it should no longer be relied on.
verdictHelp.NETWORK_UNAVAILABLE: A file or the blockchain couldn’t be reached. Try again in a moment.
